About.metaDescription: Hale is a planner for your kids’ year. Barton Dong, CEO, and Eugene Song, CTO, at Village Hale Technologies Inc.
About.lede: What’s on near the kids gets missed; mornings fill in minutes; nobody asks how it went. Hale finds it, watches the date, asks after — by text.
About.mission: Every parent should have someone who knows what’s on near them, remembers the date that fills in two minutes, and asks how it went. Across every stage of childhood, from the first months to almost grown.
About.howLede: Hale starts by finding what’s on and asking how it went. The ladder is the whole product: it climbs one rung at a time, and only when you let it.

ForCentres.getLede: A parent sends the first message — Hale never texts a family first. This is one of them, and what came back.

ForCentres.waysEyebrow: How to point a family at Hale
ForCentres.waysLede: Nothing to sign, nothing to install, and nothing for staff to keep track of.

number.title: Give them the number
number.body: Copy it and put it where parents look — a whiteboard, a handout, the back of a room sheet. A parent texts it when they are ready.

poster.title: Put up a poster
poster.body: This code opens the page that writes a parent’s first message for them. We print posters carrying your centre’s own code, so we can tell you how many families it brought — email us and we will send one.

try.title: Text it yourself first
try.body: Send the first message the way a parent would, and read what comes back, so you know what you are recommending. Reply STOP and it ends.

ForCentres.numberPending: The number is not announced yet. Email us and we will tell you when it is.
ForCentres.knowLede: A family will ask you these before they ask us.

facts.title: What Hale asks for
facts.body: First names, ages, and a postal code. The first three characters are enough — they name a town, not a street.

facts.title: Nothing is sold
facts.body: A family’s information is never sold, never shared for advertising, and never shown to another family.

facts.title: STOP ends it
facts.body: A parent texts STOP and the messages stop. They can ask for their data, or for it to be deleted, at privacy@villagehale.com.

facts.title: French, in French
facts.body: A parent can text Hale in French, and Hale answers in French.

facts.title: A child’s words stay with their parent
facts.body: Hale talks to parents. For a child of 13 or older, a parent sees the topic and a summary rather than the words — unless there is a safety concern, and then the teen is told.

ForCentres.officialEyebrow: If a family asks whether Hale is official
ForCentres.officialLine: Hale is independent. It is not run by your centre, the town, the region, or the province. It checks every registration date against the town’s own page, and if the two ever disagree, the town’s page wins.

faq.question: Does a family need an account?
faq.answer: No. A parent texts a number and Hale replies. There is no app to install, no password, and no sign-up page.

faq.question: What does it cost a family?
faq.answer: Nothing to start. Watching the dates and answering questions is free, and families who join now keep the founding rate for good.

faq.question: Do we have to sign anything?
faq.answer: No. There is no agreement, and nothing for staff to report or track. The only thing we would set up with you is a poster carrying your centre’s code.

faq.question: What does Hale refuse to do?
faq.answer: It does not diagnose and it never names a dose — a medical question goes back to your care provider. It also never fills a registration form or holds a spot on a family’s behalf. It prepares and reminds; the parent registers.

ForCentres.ctaHeading: Want a poster for your centre?
ForCentres.ctaSub: Email us and we will send one with your centre’s own code on it. A real person answers.

items.question: What is Hale?
items.answer: A planner for your kids’ year that lives in your texts. It finds what’s on near you, watches for spots, reminds you before sign-ups and asks how it went. It answers any other question you send it, too.

items.question: How do I start?
items.answer: Text the number. Hale asks where you are and how old the kids are, then shows you what’s on this week. Anything else it asks for later, only when it needs it. Hale never texts a number that hasn’t texted it first.

items.question: Do I need an app or an account?
items.answer: No. Hale works in iMessage and regular texts. The website is only there if you want to look back at what Hale has sent.

items.question: Can Hale join our group chat?
items.answer: Yes. Start a group with Hale and whoever shares the load: your co-parent, the carpool, other parents from the class. Ask in the chat and Hale answers there.

items.question: What does Hale do in a group?
items.answer: Finds a plan when someone asks, keeps track of who’s in and who’s driving, and reminds the right person the night before. Otherwise it stays quiet.

items.question: What do other parents in the group see?
items.answer: Only what’s said in that chat. Nothing from your own calendar, inbox or 1:1 texts with Hale shows up in a group.

items.question: Is my co-parent free?
items.answer: Always. Same plan, same reminders, on their own phone.

items.question: Does Hale book or register for me?
items.answer: Not yet. Hale finds the class, watches for spots and texts you the link before sign-ups open. You register yourself. Signing up for you is coming later, and only when you say yes.

items.question: What does Hale find?
items.answer: Swim, camps, drop-ins, library programs, rec classes and things to do this weekend, picked for your kids’ ages and where you live. Every find comes with the page it came from.

items.question: Can I ask it other things?
items.answer: Anything. Sleep, a rainy-day idea, what’s open Monday. Hale looks it up live and answers in a line or two.

items.question: How often will Hale text me?
items.answer: Only when there’s a reason: a heads-up before sign-ups, the link the night before, a question after the first class. Reply LESS for fewer, or STOP to end it.

items.question: Will Hale tell me if a class is any good?
items.answer: Not yet. Today Hale asks how it went, and uses your answer to pick what to send you next.

items.question: Is it free?
items.answer: Yes. Hale is free, with unlimited chat. Families who join now get every feature free until paid plans start.

items.question: What happens to our data?
items.answer: It’s never sold or used for ads. Reply STOP and the texts stop. Our privacy policy covers what Hale keeps and why, and how to have it deleted.

items.question: Is Hale a person?
items.answer: No, and it never pretends to be. Hale is built by Village Hale Technologies Inc., a small parent-founded company. Write to aloha@villagehale.com and a real person reads it.

items.question: Is Hale official?
items.answer: Hale is independent. It isn’t run by a centre, a town, a region or a province. Every date it sends comes with the source page, and if the two ever disagree, the source page wins.
